newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African individual forex limit seen 150,000 rand.
newsitem.headline: S.African individual forex limit seen 150,000 rand.

text.p: The Reserve Bank is likely initially to allow South Africans to move 150,000 rand offshore once exchange controls on individuals are partially lifted from July 1, according to life assurance giant Old Mutual.

"For some clients that would potentially be most of their money and for other clients that may be five percent," Old Mutual Investment Services (Omis) executive officer John Bryant told a media briefing.

Finance Minister Trevor Manuel announced in his March 12 budget that individuals would be allowed to invest offshore or hold foreign currency bank accounts for the first time from July. But the specific allowances have yet to be announced.
Whether South Africans would move the full amount abroad at once would depend on their individual circumstances.
"We would caution people not to take as much money out as they can without legitimate reasons," Bryant said.
Although shares on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange had been underperforming, local markets offered significantly higher returns than investments abroad.
"For example, international income funds currently show a yield of about eight percent compared to the 16 percent or so available in South Africa," he said.
"On the other hand, depreciation in the value of the rand could significantly enhance returns to South Africans invested in funds denominated in dollars or sterling."
Once exchange controls were lifted completely, Bryant said that South Africans should invest between 25 and 30 percent of their funds abroad if they were looking solely at risk diversification.
